sourceReview.excerpt:
##### **Use partitioning and place value to multiply 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers by one-digit numbers**

- Use mental strategies to multiply one-digit numbers by 10, 100, 1000
  and their multiples

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|Use place value partitioning to solve $$6 \times 500$$:|
|$$6 \times (5 \times 100)$$.|
||
|Use factorising to solve $$6 \times 500$$:|
|$$3 \times 2 \times 500$$.|
||
|Use halving to solve $$6 \times 500$$: half of 6 times 1000.|
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Estimate the product of 2 numbers (one-digit by 2- or 3-digit numbers)
  using multiples of 10 or 100

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|Such as $$684 \times 7$$ is less than $$700 \times 7\ (4900)$$.|
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Use informal written strategies such as the area model to solve
  multiplication and division problems

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|Such as $$8 \times 27$$.|
||
|![2 area model diagrams showing 8 times 27. Details in text|
|below diagram.](media/image9.png){width="3.6949682852143484in"|
|height="1.6666666666666667in"}|
||
|(area model).\|
|*Image long description*: The area model partitions 27 into its|
|place values, 20 and 7, to break down the equation into 2|
|simpler equations, 20 times 8 (160) and 7 times 8 (56). The|
|answers to these simpler equations are added to get a final|
|answer of 216.|
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Use the distributive property with the area model to partition numbers
  in representing multiplication problems

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|Such as $$684 \times 5$$.|
||
|![Area model of 684 partitioned into its place values to solve|
|684 times 5. Details|
|below.](media/image10.png){width="2.6650568678915136in"|
|height="1.6666666666666667in"}|
||
|(area model).\|
|*Image long description:* The area model partitions 684 into its|
|place values, 600, 80 and 4 to break down the equation into 2|
|simpler equations, 600 times 5 (3000), 80 times 5 (400) and 4|
|times 5 (20). The answers to these simpler equations are added|
|to get a final answer of 3420.|
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Use the distributive property with partial products to solve problems
  by multiplying the hundreds, then the tens and then the ones

+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|**Example(s):**|
||
|Such as|
|$$684 \times 3 = (600 \times 3) + (80 \times 3) + (4 \times 3)$$|
||
|$$= 1800 + 240 + 12$$|
||
|$$= 2052$$|
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

- Record the product of multiplying by a one-digit number using a formal
  algorithm
